axis_coverage.conclusion: The finite two-browser/four-candidate-plus-default matrix covers all requested proposed checks, actual output decoding and file inspection, blocked/frozen timing, cleanup, and a conditional complete Worklet pipeline. All browser work is explicitly unrun. No runtime pass is inferred. Timing oracle remains owner-defined; MIME probe/UI stop/download-click are expressly insufficient oracles.

requirements.exact_brief_clause: R1: Define permission, start/pause/resume/stop, track-ended, and cleanup behavior with an explicit error state.
requirements.analysis: Lifecycle, permission cancellation/late resolution, mute, ended, input change, final events, explicit error and teardown are covered; stream release on candidate failure conflicts with R2. M1.

requirements.exact_brief_clause: R2: Establish container/codec negotiation and fallback strategy, differentiating format support, successful construction, and successful capture/export.
requirements.analysis: Distinct format/construction/capture/export gates and finite named/default policy are present, but M1 prevents promised retry on constructor/start exceptions. Exact formats remain candidates.

requirements.exact_brief_clause: R3: Compare native recording with an AudioWorklet-based mechanism, including encoding responsibility, buffering, and scope/cost implications.
requirements.analysis: Browser encoder/muxer versus Float32 Worklet transport and owned encoder/muxer, bounded memory/backpressure, CPU/packaging costs; no custom library chosen.

requirements.exact_brief_clause: R4: Explain data-chunk timing and assembly; do not treat callback frequency as a reliable clock or claim arbitrary chunks are independently playable.
requirements.analysis: Event counts rejected; completed-Blob assembly and trailing events covered. Page timer is explicitly best effort, with five-minute requirement retained pending an owner threshold and actual decoded-duration tests.

requirements.exact_brief_clause: R5: Include a relevant released implementation/history detail and bind positive or negative capability statements to browser, version, API, operation, and conditions.
requirements.analysis: Safari 14.1/18.4/26.0, Safari 17.4 pause fix, exact two WebKit commits and pinned Chromium muxer are distinguished from unpinned current runtime support.

requirements.exact_brief_clause: R6: Specify a bounded validation matrix and clearly distinguish proposed checks from executed browser observations; disclose unsupported combinations and remaining uncertainty.
requirements.analysis: Finite matrix, actual operation evidence gates, failure scope, unsupported uncertainty, decoded-output duration and save-file inspection. Browser execution was optional and is not fabricated.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: I want record, pause, stop, playback, and download controls.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Record/pause/stop/playback/download remain component actions; resume is explicitly covered by R1.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: My draft obtains a microphone stream, constructs MediaRecorder with a single hard-coded WebM/Opus MIME string, requests a callback every second, and concatenates received chunks when stopped.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Retain microphone input and ordered completed-recording assembly; replace one hard-coded type with negotiated candidates/default; 1000 ms is a slice request, not a clock. All four embedded clauses assessed.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: It increments a duration counter on each callback and stops at 300 callbacks.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Reject 300 callbacks as duration. Final proposes monotonic active-time stop but explicitly withholds strict duration compliance through suspension pending owner threshold and validation.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: On errors it currently just resets the controls; the permission/track cleanup path is missing.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Explicit errors/cleanup replace silent reset; candidate-failure cleanup conflicts with format retries (M1).

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: I am carrying an old assumption that Safari cannot use MediaRecorder and therefore must always take a custom encoder path.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Old Safari blanket denial is disproved by Safari 14.1 vendor history; Worklet is optional rather than mandatory for all Safari.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: I also assumed that Web Audio produces WAV files automatically, that choosing a sample rate guarantees the hardware records at that rate, and that a MIME support probe proves recording will work.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Web Audio does not automatically export WAV; requested/graph rate does not prove physical hardware rate; preflight does not prove capture/export. Three embedded assumptions independently checked.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: These assumptions have not been verified against a selected released browser.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Unpinned exact browser/OS runtime behavior is left unverified; release/source evidence is separately bounded.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: Please research them rather than treating them as required product restrictions.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Investigates false assumptions as research questions, not product restrictions.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: The fallback sketch uses an AudioWorklet to collect raw samples and keeps all samples until stop, then encodes a WAV download.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Custom PCM/WAV path compared but not selected; raw accumulation must be capped and an encoder/container supplied. Native remains bounded first choice.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: I have not budgeted memory for five minutes, resolved channel layout, chosen an encoder, or addressed a page suspension.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Memory math 48,000×300×1×4=57,600,000 bytes (54.93 MiB); PCM16 payload=28,800,000 bytes. Rate/channels multiply cost. Encoder/layout choice deferred because no Worklet implementation selected; page suspension and cap explicitly investigated.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: A format fallback should preserve the user's capture capability where support exists, but the page must honestly explain an unsupported operation.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Advertised native candidate/default fallback supports this intention, but R1 destroys the live track on the exact constructor/start-exception path R2 needs (M1). Honest unsupported messages otherwise defined.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: No new upload service is allowed.
Keep R1–R6 and the negative constraints binding.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: All R1–R6 and eight negative constraints remain explicit; R2 coherence fails M1.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: The revision needs explicit track cleanup, a truthful duration rule, format selection with failure handling, and a bounded buffer/export policy.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Cleanup, duration honesty and bounded export are developed. Format failure handling remains incoherent under M1. Duration meaning/threshold are disclosed release decisions, not a false completed guarantee. All four embedded needs assessed.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: It may choose native capture for some combinations and a fallback or explicit refusal for others if the evidence justifies that boundary.
exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Native-first and explicit refusal without unselected custom encoder are justified for a small component. Refusal must not be conflated with failure to exercise the promised native fallback (M1).

exact_plan_dispositions.independent_assessment: Does not require identical quality or cross-browser playback; same-browser preview and optional external-player tests are scoped correctly.

material_findings.title: Constructor/start cleanup makes the promised native-format retry unavailable
exact_candidate_text: A constructor or synchronous `start()` exception releases the stream and reports `error`.
If failure occurs before any nonempty chunk and the track is still live, finalize that recorder and try the next candidate.
material_findings.analysis: The first instruction is unconditional. Its cleanup semantics stop acquired tracks, while the second requires a live track. Thus a named-format constructor/start failure before bytes reaches terminal microphone cleanup instead of the stated remaining-candidate/default attempt. The plan specifies no reacquisition step for that retry. This is an internal plan conflict, not a claim that code was implemented or a browser failed.
material_findings.source_backed_inference: App track.stop ends the track. A stream with all tracks ended is inactive. MediaRecorder.start rejects an inactive stream. A fresh recorder cannot make the stopped microphone track live.
material_findings.materiality: R2 and exact original P11 require a coherent fallback that preserves capture where supported. The explicitly anticipated constructor/start-failure-despite-probe path cannot follow the advertised finite fallback, even in a permitted case where another native format or the UA default would be viable on the original live stream. No nonexistent deployment or requirement to build a custom fallback is assumed.
material_findings.lineage: Present in investigator draft; not detected in the independent critique; retained verbatim in final. It is not one of the corrected F1/F3 defects.
material_findings.counterinterpretation_considered: R2 could be intended as an exception to R1, or error cleanup could be intended only after all retries. The final states neither exception and expressly makes constructor/start failure release the stream. Guessing that precedence or an unmentioned reacquisition would repair the plan rather than assess its actual instructions.

limits.detail: Exact target Chrome/Safari build/OS, offered MIME strings and actual permission/capture/playback/download behavior remain untested. Browser execution was optional, so no invented deployment or browser test obligation is imposed.

Five-minute active/output/wall-clock meaning and permissible overrun need an owner decision; the final retains the requirement, documents timer insufficiency and proposes decoded-output threshold checks. This qualification is not itself a remaining material error.

Final correction table calls independent playability of every Blob a released assumption/gap, but the exact user plan only proposed concatenation. R4 explicitly requires the chunk-playability caution, so coverage is correct; the attribution is imprecise.

Safari 18.4 Ogg sentence announces OS-scoped container support without explicitly saying MediaRecorder output; the final treats Ogg as a candidate requiring exact audio-only runtime checks, so it does not claim a supported Ogg recorder. Safari 18.4/26.0 ALAC overlap remains acknowledged.

Web Audio configurable render quantum is checked in the 2026-09-22 Working Draft. The final says actual buffer length should govern and does not claim all target browsers expose the newest configuration properties.

Candidate source directories contain authored indexes, not captured original primary-page responses. They were read in full; this reviewer independently saved current primary retrievals. Those cannot prove the exact webpage bytes seen at candidate access time.
